sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, ANU. (Sukurum phonology: sec. 4.2.4, pp. 52-53)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.2.4 gives only a phoneme table (Table 4.5) and 7 notes on allophony/dialect variants (Wangat prenasalised voiceless stops, Gabagiap [c]/[nc], /h/ rare, /b/ word-final [b]~[β], /g/ = [ɣ], /k/ back velar). Ch. 4 intro says 'Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date'. The words 'stress'/'unstressed' occur in the book only re folk perceptions of dialect difference (p. c.3.3), an Adzera vowel-sequence note, a Duwet allophone, and a South/North Watut historical note; no stress rule for Sukurum or any Upper Markham language.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne C. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham and Ramu Valleys, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. (Sukurum: sec. 4.2.4, pp. 103-104)
sources.note: Nothing; sec. 4.2.4 is word-for-word the same phoneme table and notes as the 1989 book. No stress/accent statement anywhere for Sukurum.
